issues.failure_explanation: The localized CBS dynamics depend essentially on gamma, but the lemma quantifies only alpha, beta, kappa, and lambda. Its proof silently imposes gamma = 2 alpha'/(alpha'+1). For other gamma values the drift and moment equations differ, so the asserted time-rescaled equivalence does not follow.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the proof's required condition $\gamma=2\alpha'/(\alpha'+1)$ to the lemma and verify the time-rescaling under that parameter choice.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed equivalence with classical CBS is false for the unrestricted localized CBS dynamics stated in the lemma.
issues.title: Equivalence lemma omits the required value of gamma
issues.why_classification: The source itself supplies the missing parameter value, and adding it is a short local restriction that preserves the equivalence claim in its intended regime.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any choice of the CBS parameter\footnote{We write $\alpha'$ for the CBS parameter to distinguish it from the $\alpha$ parameter of localized CBS.} $\alpha' > 0$
a weighted covariance $\mathbf C_{U,t} = \mathcal C_{\alpha, \lambda \mathcal C(\rho_t)}(\rho_t; U_t)$ with scalars $\alpha\ge0$ and $\lambda > 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma permits every alpha>0 independently of alpha'>0, but its formula gives lambda<0 when alpha<alpha' and is undefined when alpha=alpha'. This violates the earlier requirement lambda>0 and can destroy the positive-definite Gaussian localization kernel and preconditioner used by the dynamics.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the finite-lambda statement to $\alpha>\alpha'$. If the boundary case is desired, formulate and prove it separately as the limit $\lambda\to\infty$.
issues.overall_effect: The equivalence lemma is not even well-defined over a substantial part of its stated parameter range.
issues.title: The prescribed localization parameter can be nonpositive or undefined
issues.why_classification: A local parameter restriction restores a valid preconditioner while retaining the same equivalence construction for freely selectable alpha greater than alpha'.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: randomly subsamples particles with a factor $\nu\in(0, 1]$

U_{n+1}^i = U_n^i + \Bigl[-\frac\gamma\kappa\Bigl(U_n^i - \widehat\mu_{\beta,\kappa\widehat{\mathbf C}/\beta}^{(\nu,i)}(\bm U_n; U_n^i)\Bigr) + \nabla_{u^i}\cdot\widehat{\mathbf C}\Bigr]\dt + \sqrt{2\dt}\,\widehat{\mathbf C}^{1/2}\xi_n^i,

issues.failure_explanation: For any nu<1, all J-1 eligible particles are rejected with probability $(1-\nu)^{J-1}>0$. On that event both sums vanish and the weighted mean is 0/0, so the next algorithmic update is undefined. More generally, zero target weights can also make the denominator vanish.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify a nonempty batching rule, such as sampling a fixed positive batch size or resampling until at least one eligible positive-weight particle is selected, together with a fallback for an all-zero weight set.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised randomized localized CBS procedure is not a well-defined stochastic algorithm on its stated parameter range, and runs using random batching can fail with positive probability.
issues.title: Random-batch mean can divide by zero
issues.why_classification: A standard local modification of batch selection and zero-weight handling makes every update well-defined without changing the method's drift, rate, or intended scope.
